notes:
Viewing, comparing, restoring and deleting a snapshot work again — all four failed. A snapshot could also go missing from the list when a background autosave and a manual snapshot or deletion landed at the same moment.

Moving, trashing or restoring a document no longer drops it out of search until its next save, and renaming one no longer leaves the old title and path behind in the results.

The backup interval you choose in Settings is now saved, checked and applied within a minute. Before, it was ignored and forgotten on restart.

Setting the mascot's frequency to Off now keeps it quiet.

Your own saves are no longer reported as edits made outside Corylus. On macOS every save came back as an external change, which is exactly the false “modified externally” warning this check exists to prevent.

Switching projects no longer carries a document from the project you just closed into the new one's binder.

On Windows, a file added to a project folder outside Corylus now appears straight away instead of only after reopening the project.

A project downloaded from the cloud now arrives with its binder: chapters keep their order and their place in folders. Before, the copy rebuilt the binder from the files on disk, so chapters could come out in the wrong order and a later sync could treat the copy as a separate project.

The sync engine (rclone) now stops when Corylus closes, even after a crash or a forced quit. Before, it could keep running in the background; any copy left behind from an earlier session is stopped the next time sync starts.
